The captioned writ petition is filed by the helpless father seeking mandamus to the Land Acquisition Officer to release compensation amount in his favour.
2. Facts leading to the case are that, petitioner was arrayed as defendant No.1 in O.S.No.61/2017.
The said suit was filed by one of the daughters of the petitioner herein seeking relief of partition and separate possession.
This Court in W.P.Nos.110234-110235/2017 pursuant to joint compromise petition filed by the parties, disposed off the petition recording compromise between the parties.

It would be useful for this court to cull out the relevant paragraphs 7, 8, 9, 14 and 16, which reads as under:
"7. Property Bearing No.112/3:
measuring 2 Acres 3 guntas situated at Budni NC: 2023:KHC-D:9021 B.K. village and this property is exclusively allotted to share of Balappa i.e., Defendant No.1/respondent No.4.
8.

measuring 5 Acres 6 guntas situated at Budni B.K. village and this property is exclusively allotted to share or Balappa i.e., Defendant No.1/respondent No.4.

14. House Properties: VPC No.41, 41/1, 41/2 all three houses are situated at Budni B.K. village and all the three houses are allotted to the share of Balappa.

16. And further submits that the respondent No.4 i.e., defendant No.1 has agreed that the properties which were allotted to him has to be equally divided amongst Basavaraj and Venkappa after his demise."
If these clauses of compromise petition are looked into, respondent No.8, who is one of the son of the petitioner, is taking advantage of clause No.16.

Under clause No.16, the parites have resolved that after demise of present petitioner, Sy. No.112/3 measuring 2 acres 3 guntas, Sy. No.4/1 measuring 5 acres 6 guntas, Sy. No.112/5 measuring 37 guntas and Sy. No.86/2 measuring 7 acres 21 guntas, which are exclusively allotted to the share of the petitioner, would devolve upon his two sons.
4. Based on this clause, respondent No.3 is objecting for release of compensation in favour of the petitioner.

It is not in dispute that the petition properties bearing Sy. No.4/1 measuring 5 acres 6 guntas, Sy. No.112/3 measuring 2 acres 3 guntas and 112/5 measuring 37.08 guntas are acquired for Upper Krishna Project by respondent Nos.1 and 2.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:9021 5.
It is also borne out from the records that respondent No.3 has filed injunction suit restraining the petitioner from alienating the suit schedule property.

If these significant details are looked into, I am of the view that respondent No.3, who is son of the petitioner herein, cannot dispute the title of the petitioner over the property bearing Sy. No.112/3.

This Court has to bear in mind the petitioner,
who is the Senior Citizen, is aged 72 years and the lands, which were allotted to his share exclusively are acquired by respondent Nos.1 and 2.
Therefore, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are required to complete the acquisition proceedings and pass award and pay compensation to the petitioner, who is legally entitled to receive compensation.

6. In the light of the compromise recorded in W.P.Nos.110234-110235/2017, the petitioner has acquired absolute title over the petition property and therefore, he alone is entitled to receive the compensation.
Therefore, the petitioner has legal right to NC: 2023:KHC-D:9021 insist and request the Acquiring Authority to pass award and deposit the compensation amount.
He is also entitled to seek enhancement of the compensation amount in the event award is passed and is found to be inadequate.
7. In the light of the observations made supra, I am of the view that the writ petition succeeds.
